note:
John T Brewster, solicitor, his wife Elizabeth and two servants at 17 Park Terrace (#256) on the 1891 return, transcribed by A. Hagues. None of the four was in the record, and 17 Park Terrace held only 1921 (the Newmarshes), so 1891 is free.

**This completes the Italian Villas trio.** Wright's Directory prints 'John Brewster, solicitor' at 17 Park Terrace in 1894-95 and 'Italian villas, John Thompson Brewster, (solr)' there in 1898-99 - the 1898-99 volume putting the group name against 15, 16 and 17 together. With Joseph F Youngman now confirmed at 15 and William F Bromley at 16 by the 1891 census, all three houses the directory calls Italian Villas are confirmed at their numbers from the census side as well.

The directory also gives his middle name, Thompson, which this return abbreviates to T; it is not added to his name here, since a directory line is not the same authority as a return for a person's name. His widow stayed on: 'Brewster Mrs. Elizabeth' is printed at 17 in 1910-11, so Elizabeth H Brewster, born at Ostend in Belgium about 1835, held the house for at least twenty years after this census.

**Probably a brother of the Frederick Brewster at 10 Park Terrace.** Frederick Brewster (#720, born 1834, clerk to the tax commissioners) was lodging at 10 Park Terrace on this same 1891 return, and both men were born in the parish of St Nicholas, Nottingham, five years apart. That is suggestive and no more, so no family link is made and neither is bound to the other. Mary and Eliza R Morton, the two servants, were both born at Derby and are seven years apart, so they may well be sisters, but the return does not say so. Ages are as the enumerator wrote them, so a birth year worked back from one may be a year out either way.
source: 1891 census, 17 Park Terrace, transcribed by A. Hagues. Directory evidence: Wright's Directory of Nottingham 1894-95, page 107 (Leicester Special Collections id 164613); 1898-99, page 115 (id 165291); 1910-11, page 154 (id 165830).
